title: Choose the visual world for CEVDA
question: The roll assigned the Boletín direction. Keep it, take the living schoolbook pick or an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Boletín de calificaciones
options.lineage: Dominican school report cards and stamped certificates
options.thesis: The school introduces itself the way it reports on a child: a ruled, signed, stamped record of what each level gives.
options.viewport: A full-width boletín sheet: crest seal top left, the school name as the header row, levels and ages as the first graded rows, Admisión as the stamped action.
options.risk: Grades imply judgment; if the grid is set coldly, a warm school reads like a bureaucracy.

raised.raise: Hierarchy is carried by type size alone; rows never need icons or boxes to rank.
Exactly three brand colors, committed to whole regions, never scattered.
The chosen level renders solid while the others stay dashed, one state grammar sitewide.

options.label: Living schoolbook
options.lineage: Notebooks, gold-star stickers, and highlighters from a Dominican classroom
options.thesis: The site is a school notebook come alive: the crest's royal blue fills whole pages, and gold stars, pencils, and highlighter swipes move with a child's energy.
options.viewport: Split hero: a two-line display headline with a highlighter swipe on one word, two pill CTAs, and a draggable polaroid stack of real school photos ringed by floating stickers.
options.risk: The familiar school-stationery look; it needs full commitment to avoid reading as a kids' template.

options.label: Festival lineup sheet
options.thesis: Everything the school offers billed like a festival lineup, where size alone says what matters.
options.viewport: A blue sheet: the school name spans the width, the levels as headliners, extracurriculars packed into a justified block.
options.case: Holds product clarity (offerings read instantly) but parents do not see their child's school in a gig poster.
options.risk: No photos means no faces, and trust depends on the faces.

options.label: Sapeur portrait plate
options.thesis: Each child in uniform as a captioned portrait plate.
options.viewport: A full-length portrait on a flat backdrop with a ruled caption.
options.case: Loses both axes: posed portraits of minors are not what parents browse for.

options.label: Sewing pattern envelope
options.thesis: Levels as lettered views on a pattern envelope.
options.viewport: An envelope front with views A and B for Inicial and Primario.
options.case: Loses both axes: a craft metaphor with no link to schooling.
options.kept: Chosen option solid, the rest dashed.

options.label: Bioluminescent wake
options.thesis: Light that follows the visitor across a dark sea.
options.viewport: A dark field where the pointer draws glowing trails.
options.case: Loses both axes: dark and abstract where parents want daylight and faces.
options.risk: Heavy GPU work on mid-range phones.
options.kept: Only the active element carries light.

options.label: Cracktro scroller
options.thesis: Rank as depth over a drifting void.
options.viewport: One ivory line over drifting dust.
options.case: Loses both axes: no cultural link to families or schools.

options.label: Split-flap board
options.thesis: Schedules as a flipping departure board.
options.viewport: A departure board of class times.
options.case: Loses both axes: the school is not a timetable.
options.kept: A fixed grid where only cells change.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A private school homepage done straight: photo hero, program cards, testimonials, contact.
canonCard.viewport: Full-width photo hero with the name and two buttons, then program cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other school site by design.
